links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses (FRE and SMOG) on urinary incontinence questions
links.quote: DeepSeek also demonstrated superior readability, as indicated by a higher Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) score (76.43 ± 10.90 vs. 70.95 ± 11.16, P = 0.039) and a lower Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG) index (12.26 ± 1.39 vs. 14.21 ± 1.88, P < 0.001), suggesting easier comprehension.

links.outcome: Provision of source references in chatbot responses (mDISCERN)
links.effect: Both chatbots rarely provided source references; mDISCERN 28.24 ± 0.88 (DeepSeek) vs 28.76 ± 1.56 (ChatGPT-4.0), P = 0.188.
links.quote: Both AI chatbots rarely provided source references.

links.outcome: Guideline adherence of chatbot responses to AUA/SUFU and EAU urinary incontinence guidelines
links.effect: Fully compliant responses: DeepSeek 11 (73.33%), ChatGPT-4.0 13 (86.67%), P = 0.651; occasional deviations observed.
links.quote: Regarding guideline adherence, DeepSeek had 11 (73.33%) fully compliant responses, while ChatGPT-4.0 had 13 (86.67%), with no significant difference [P = 0.651, Cohen's w = 0.083 (95% CI: 0.021, 0.232)].

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks and compares the performance (reliability, readability, guideline adherence) of two LLMs (DeepSeek and ChatGPT-4.0) on 25 guideline-based questions about urinary incontinence without testing any organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
